chunks.title: engine
chunks.text:
# The engine model (how a uxn·forge game is built)

GameMaker/Godot-style: **scenes** hold **objects**, objects come from
**templates**, and behaviour is **events → actions** (the Blocks
view). Scripts (`.ux` modules) hold the logic that blocks are too
coarse for, and blocks call into them. The engine compiles everything
to one ETAL program (`main.ux` + your scripts).

chunks.title: Pieces
chunks.text:
## Pieces
* **Sprite**: art. 1×1 to 4×4 tiles of 8×8, 4 colors (indices 0–3).
  A sprite can be a **sheet** (`set_sheet`): an object shows one
  **cell**, and actions switch cells.
* **Template** (`create_object_def`): an object type, like "piece" or
  "enemy". It has default sprite and kind, **variables** (each instance
  keeps its own copy: `add_template_var`) and **events**.
* **Object / instance**: a template placed in a scene
  (`place_instance`), or an inline object (`put_on_scene`), which is
  its own one-off template. Instances keep their own position and
  variable overrides.
* **Scene**: a level or screen. It has objects, its own **scene
  events** (the level controller: start, keys, timers, clicks
  anywhere), and a **spawn pool** (free slots for `spawn` actions).
  `p.start` is the first scene. Text objects (`set_label`) draw
  strings; a `text` action redraws them with a number.
* **Game variables** (`add_variable`): global u16 values, `var_<id>[0]`
  in code. **Template variables**: per-instance u16, `iv_<name>[self]`
  in code.

chunks.title: Levels bigger than the screen
chunks.text:
## Levels bigger than the screen
* **Tile layer** (`set_tilemap`): a scene's grid of 8×8 cells from a
  tile sheet (a sprite whose cells are 1×1 tiles). One byte per cell,
  no object slots, so a 160×18 level is cheap. Listed cells are
  **solid** for movement. The layer sets the scene's world size.
  Users paint it in the Scene view (Tiles → paint).
* **Camera** (`set_camera`): follows the first live instance of a
  template, centered and clamped to the world. Objects marked **HUD**
  (`set_hud`) stay fixed on screen (scores, lives).
* **Movement presets** (`set_movement`) on a template:
  `platformer` (arrows run, up/A/space jumps, gravity; solid tiles and
  solid objects block) and `walker` (patrols, turns at walls and
  ledges: enemies). The `jump {power}` action launches either one
  upward (stomp bounces, springs). Mouse coordinates stay
  screen-space.

chunks.title: Events (triggers)
chunks.text:
## Events (triggers)
create (scene starts / spawned), step (every frame), destroy,
key (named input or a controller button), click (pressed on this
object; on a scene: anywhere), release (mouse released anywhere),
collide (with any|solid|player|movable|def:<id>; the hit one is
`other`), alarm (timer 0–3, armed by `wait`), message (sent by `send`
to every object and the scene). Scenes have no collide/destroy.

chunks.title: Actions (all values are u16 expressions)
chunks.text:
## Actions (all values are u16 expressions)
move, set_pos, glide (tween over frames), sprite, cell, look (blend,
flips), show/hide, text, play (sound), song/song_stop, goto (switch
scene), overlay (open a scene on top and freeze the one below: pause
menus) / back, wait (timer → alarm), destroy (self|other|def),
spawn (new instance of a template), send (message), set (game var or
my/other var: set/add/sub), if/else, repeat, **call** (a script
function), code (raw ETAL, last resort).
Values: numbers, variables, `my`/`other` vars, x/y/cell/w/h of self or
other, mouse x/y, random, math, and **function calls** (script fns
that return u16). Conditions: compare, button held, touching, mouse
over, mouse down, all/any/not.

**Rule of thumb:** placement, art, sound, input, scene flow and
simple state go in blocks. Rules, AI, tables and anything with loops
over data go in a script function that blocks `call`.

chunks.title: Scripts ↔ engine contract
chunks.text:
## Scripts ↔ engine contract
* Scripts are imported after the engine's state, so they can read and
  write it. Public runtime names (slot arrays have 128 entries,
  indexed by slot; `self` is the running object's slot, `other` is the
  collide partner):
  `ox[s] oy[s]` (u16 position), `ocell[s]` (u16 cell), `odef[s]` (u8
  template index), `oflags[s]` (u8: bit0 alive, bit1 solid, bit2
  movable, bit3 visible, bit4 player), `ocount`, `scene` (u8 current
  scene id, compare with `SC_<SCENE>` constants), `scene_go`,
  `var_<id>[0]`, `iv_<name>[slot]`.
* Functions called from blocks take **u16 params only** and return
  **u16** when used as a value (`-> u16`). Keep them small: every
  param is a permanent zero-page byte.
* Optional hooks in `custom.ux` (`set_custom_code`):
  `custom_setup()` (boot), `custom_frame()` (each frame),
  `custom_draw()` (after drawing: HUDs), `custom_key()` /
  `custom_mouse()` (inside the vectors; latches only).
* **Reserved names** (declaring them is an error): anything starting
  `e_`, `spr_`, `var_`, `iv_`, `SC_`, plus `ox oy ot om ow oh otw oth
  osw oflags odef osp ocell omx omy omw omh otx onv onf ogx ogy ogn
  oan oaf oak oad oa0-3 st0-3 ocount scene

chunks.title: Limits that shape designs
chunks.text:
## Limits that shape designs
128 object slots in total; the per-scene spawn pool is reserved
from those. Collide pairs unroll per scene (keep targets narrow).
4 audio voices; songs hold up to 16 steps per voice. Zero page is
256 bytes and the engine uses much of it, so big games keep state in
`buffer` arrays. Colors: 4 palette entries (`set_theme`); blends
0/5/10/15 make color 0 transparent (pieces on a board use blend 0
or 5).

chunks.title: Workflow the agent must follow
chunks.text:
## Workflow the agent must follow
1. The project summary at the top of each request is current. Use it,
   and call `describe` / `scene_map` / `read_file` for details instead
   of guessing ids.
2. Plan in terms of templates, events and scripts before editing.
3. Make the edits with tools. Read scripts before rewriting them
   (`read_file`) and keep what you don't need to change.
4. `validate` (instant, local), then `check_build` (real compiler),
   and fix every error it names, repeating until clean.
5. Reply with a short summary of what changed and how to try it
   (Playtest).

chunks.title: etal
chunks.text:
# ETAL language reference (what scripts are written in)

ETAL is a typed language that compiles to Uxntal for the Uxn VM.
Every expression leaves exactly `sizeof(type)` bytes on the stack.
Source of truth: `uxn-dsl/docs/language/*.md`. When unsure, write the
code, run `check_build`, and fix what the compiler says.

chunks.title: Types
chunks.text:
## Types
`u8` (1 byte), `u16` (2 bytes, big-endian), `bool` (0/1), `i8`/`i16`
(two's complement; no signed `/` or `%`), `u8 mod N` / `u16 mod N`
(every store wraps into [0,N)), `[N] T` fixed arrays, `&T` addresses,
structs. Literals take the smallest type that fits (0–255 is `u8`).
Arithmetic and bitwise ops give `u8` only when BOTH sides are `u8`,
otherwise `u16`. Comparisons give `bool`. `&&`/`||` are bitwise and
evaluate both sides (no short-circuit).

**No implicit narrowing.** `u8 → u16` widens automatically, but a
`u16` into a `u8` is a type error. The narrowing bridge is a mod type:

```ux
to8 :: fn(v: u16) -> u8 {
    t: u16 mod 256 = v;
    return t;
}
```

Masking (`v & 255`) still yields `u16`, so it does not narrow.
There are no casts and a `u16` never becomes a pointer.

chunks.title: Declarations (the second symbol decides mutability)
chunks.text:
## Declarations (the second symbol decides mutability)
```ux
x: u16;              ( mutable, zero-page )
x: u16 = 5;          ( mutable with initializer, runs at boot )
n: u16 = 0;          ( prefer explicit types over `n := 0` )
LIMIT : u16 : 20;    ( typed constant with storage )
WIDTH :: 20;         ( free constant: the label IS the value )
buffer board[64]: u8;     ( main RAM array, global only )
grid: [16] u8;            ( small zero-page array )
data tile = [ 0x3c, 66, 129 ];   ( ROM bytes; &tile is its address; tile[i] reads )
Point :: struct { x: u16; y: u8; };   buffer pts[32]: Point;   pts[i].x = 4;
group pos: u8 { x: u8  y: u8 }        ( zero-page struct, .pos/x )
meta { title: "Game", author: "me" }  ( once per program )
import "rules.ux"                      ( splice another file; include-once )
```

Only GLOBAL arrays/buffers are indexable (no local arrays, no array
literals, no bounds checks). Arrays copy whole with `=` when type and
length match; otherwise they never touch the stack.

chunks.title: Functions, events, macros
chunks.text:
## Functions, events, macros
```ux
add :: fn(a: u16, b: u16) -> u16 { return a + b; }
on_frame :: event() { step(); }     ( a vector handler: ends with BRK )
macro clamp8(v: u16) -> u16 { return v & 255; }   ( inlined, type-checked )
```

* Valued fns MUST `return expr;` on every path (falling off the end
  returns garbage).
* Arguments widen `u8 → u16` at the call site; arity is checked;
  call order is free (signatures are collected first).
* **No recursion and no reentrancy**: params and locals are static
  zero-page bytes. A fn calling itself corrupts its own locals.
* Calling a valued fn as a bare statement warns; write `_ = f();`.
* Events return with bare `return;` only.

chunks.title: Statements
chunks.text:
## Statements
`if c { } elif c { } else { }`, `while c { }`,
`for i in 0..n { }` (half-open; `i` is always u16; a pure bound is read
once), `match v { 0 => { } 1 => { } _ => { } }` (integer literals,
lowers to an if-chain), `x += 1;` (all compound ops), `goto l;` /
`label l;` (same fn), `assert c;`, `rpush x;` / `rpop;` (return stack),
`raw { TAL }` (escape hatch; unchecked). Comments are `( … )`. Strings exist only as literals for `print("…")`. Escapes are
`\n \t \\ \"`.

chunks.title: Devices
chunks.text:
## Devices
Ports are typed: `Screen.x = 10;`, `b: u8 = Controller.button;`.
Writing a sprite reads `addr/x/y/auto` at the moment `sprite` is
written, so set those first. The engine declares every Varvara device
(System, Console, Screen, Controller, Mouse, Audio0-3, DateTime).
Never redeclare one.

chunks.title: Budgets: these are the real failure modes
chunks.text:
## Budgets: these are the real failure modes
* **Zero page: 256 bytes.** Every global scalar, every fn param and
  every local takes bytes for the whole program. The engine already
  uses part of it. Prefer `buffer x[1]: u16;` (RAM, read `x[0]`) for
  state, and reuse a few scratch globals instead of naming many locals.
  The error is `zero-page overflow`.
* **Label dictionary (`Symbols exceeded`).** Every fn, data blob,
  buffer and branch is a label. In big programs, use fewer and shorter
  fns, flatten nested ifs with `&&`, and prefer one sprite sheet over
  many sprites.
* **References per fn (~1200)**: split giant fns.
* Unused `data` or globals give warnings. Delete them.
* Drifblim rejects some label names that look like hex (`a1`, `f66`)
  and `face`. Use distinctive names.

chunks.title: Input facts
chunks.text:
## Input facts
`Controller.key` self-clears right after its vector fires, so polling
in the frame never sees it; latch it in a key vector. The engine
already does this, so engine code reads input through events or the
`held` condition. D-pad bits: 1 A, 2 B, 4 select, 8 start, 16 up,
32 down, 64 left, 128 right. Key codes: 32 space, 27 escape, 13 enter.
Mouse `state & 1` is the left button.

chunks.title: Common compiler errors → fix
chunks.text:
## Common compiler errors → fix
* `type mismatch: u16 vs u8` → widen the target to u16, or narrow
  with `to8` above.
* `unknown identifier` → declare it (globals before use in that file)
  or `import` the module that has it.
* `discarded return value` → `_ = f();`.
* `zero-page overflow` → move scalars into `buffer name[1]` and cut
  locals/params.
* `Symbols exceeded` / `References exceeded` → fewer labels, split fns.
* `duplicate definition` → the name is already declared (in another
  script, a library module, or the engine; see reserved names in
  engine.md).

chunks.title: examples
chunks.text:
# Example: chess in the engine model (the pattern to imitate)

The Chess example (read-only; "Duplicate to edit") is built the way
the engine intends. Use it as the reference for "blocks for the
game's shape, scripts for its rules".

* **Scenes**: `menu` (title + PLAY button), `side` (WHITE/BLACK
  buttons set game var `side`), `play` (board tiles, 32 pieces, text
  objects title/turn/score, FLIP and MENU buttons, `pool: 28` spawn
  slots for move dots), `pause` and `over`. `pause` and `over` open
  with `overlay` so the board stays frozen underneath; RESUME/Esc use
  `back`. Inputs: `confirm` (Enter) and `pause` (Esc).
* **Art**: `board4` (32×32 board tile used by `tile`), a `pieces`
  sheet (one cell per piece kind and color), `dot`, `cursor`.
* **Templates**:
  * `tile`: board squares.
  * `piece` (blend 0, template var `sq`): on create it sets
    `sq = layout_sq(x, y)`, calls `put_piece(my sq, cell + 1)` and
    snaps to `sq_x/sq_y`. Each step, if `grabbed_sq() == my sq`, it
    follows the mouse. On message `moved`: if it was captured it
    destroys itself; if it moved, it sets `sq = move_to()`, glides to

chunks.title: Example: Sprout Run (platformer, no scripts)
chunks.text:
## Example: Sprout Run (platformer, no scripts)
* Scenes `title`, `level`, `win`, `lose`. `level` has a 160×18 tile
  layer (sheet `tiles`: grass, dirt, brick, stone are solid; bush,
  flower and fence are decor), `camera: follow hero`, and a HUD text
  object `hud`.
* Templates: `hero` (platformer, speed 2, jump 5, mask 2,3,12×13,
  blend 5), `beetle` (walker, speed 1), `coin`, `flag`.
* Hero events: collide coin → destroy other, coins +1, play coin, send
  `score` (the HUD redraws `COINS ` + var coins on that message).
  Collide beetle → if `my y + 12 < other y` (falling onto it):
  destroy other, jump 3, play stomp; else play hurt and goto lose.
  Collide flag → goto win. Step: if y > 144 (fell in a pit) → lose.
* Level scene create: set coins 0.

chunks.title: Small patterns
chunks.text:
## Small patterns
* **Score HUD**: game var `score`; a text object `hud` "SCORE"; on a
  coin's collide with player: set score add 1, then `text` on hud
  with value var score, then destroy self.
* **Timer spawner**: scene create: wait 60 slot 0. Scene alarm 0:
  spawn enemy at (random 160, 0), then wait 60 slot 0 again.
* **Pause**: scene key escape → overlay pause. Pause scene key escape →
  back.
* **Script value**: `dist :: fn(a: u16, b: u16) -> u16 { if a > b {
  return a - b; } return b - a; }` used in an if condition: compare
  `call dist(my x, other x)` lt 16.

chunks.title: tools
chunks.text:
# Agent tools: how to use them together

Source of truth: `frontend/src/lib/agent/tools.ts`. Each tool's own
description and params travel with the request; this page covers how
they combine. Tools edit the open project in the user's tab (the same
store the UI edits), so the user sees every change live.

chunks.title: Looking before acting
chunks.text:
## Looking before acting
* The request starts with a **project summary** (scenes, templates,
  events, scripts, sprites, sounds, variables). Trust it for ids.
* `describe` gives a compact snapshot again (after many edits).
* `scene_map {scene?}` gives positions and sizes of every object;
  `find_space` / `check_space` find free spots.
* `read_file {path, from?, to?}` returns numbered source: a script
  (`chess.ux`), `custom.ux`, a generated file (`main.ux`) or a
  library module (`lib/fix16.ux`). Read a script before editing it.
* `list_library {module?}` lists the standard modules or one module's
  exports.
* `preview_event` shows the ETAL an event lowers to.

chunks.title: Building
chunks.text:
## Building
* Art: `create_sprite` (pixels 0–3), `set_sheet`, `set_look`,
  `add_anim_frame` / `set_anim`, `set_theme` (the 4 colors).
* Things: `create_object_def` (template), `add_template_var`,
  `place_instance`, `put_on_scene` (one-off object), `extract_object`,
  `set_label` (text objects), `move_object`, `rename_object`,
  `delete_node`, `reorder_nodes`, `move_node`, `nest_scene`.
* Scenes: `create_scene`, `add_transition` (click/key → goto).
* Behaviour: `add_event {def|object|scene, trigger, …}` returns the
  event id; `add_action {…, event, action: JSON}` appends an action.
  Nested bodies go inline (`then`, `else`, `body`) or via `path`
  (`"2.then"`). Use `delete_event`, `delete_action` and
  `preview_event` to iterate.
* State: `add_variable` / `set_variable` / `rename_variable` /
  `delete_variable` (game vars), `add_template_var` (per instance).
* Sound: `create_sound` + `set_sound_voice`, `create_song` +
  `set_song_note` / `set_song_vol`; `play` / `song` actions use them.
* Code: `write_script {path, code}` (whole module, created or
  replaced), `delete_script`, `set_custom_code` (hooks),
  `set_loop` (engine | script).

chunks.title: Checking (always, before saying "done")
chunks.text:
## Checking (always, before saying "done")
1. `validate`: instant local checks (ids, references, reserved
   names, budgets the editor knows).
2. `check_build`: compiles with the real ETAL compiler on the server
   and returns `{file, line, msg}` diagnostics mapped to the user's
   files. Fix each one (`read_file` around the line, then
   `write_script`) and check again. Stop after 3 failed rounds and
   tell the user what is still wrong.
3. `emit_files` only when you need to see all of the generated code.

Export and playtest are UI buttons; tell the user to press Playtest.

chunks.title: varvara
chunks.text: # Varvara context (verified against uxn2/src/uxn2.c)

chunks.title: Screen
chunks.text:
## Screen
* One sprite-port write draws exactly one 8×8 tile (2bpp = 16
  bytes: 8 channel-one rows, then 8 channel-two rows). Bigger art =
  consecutive tiles: the Screen/auto port draws N extra tiles in one
  write (length nibble, row/col direction, auto-addr advances 8 or 16
  bytes per tile) — or just repeat addr+sprite writes per tile, which
  is what our emitter does (no auto-port dependency, portable to
  every emulator). Sprite byte: bit7 = 2bpp, bit6 = layer, bits5-4 =
  flips, low nibble = blend.
* Blend LUT row 1 is identity `{0,1,2,3}` and opaque — so mode **129**
  (0x81) draws true 4-color 2bpp sprites. Index 0 is NOT transparent
  there; it paints palette 0. (Blend 0 skips index 0 but collapses
  index 1 into palette 0 — wrong for full-color art.)
* No cursor is drawn by the VM — games blit their own (`SDL_ShowCursor`
  off). Coordinates are window pixels: at zoom ≠ 1, hit-tests
  miscalibrate by the zoom factor (upstream behavior).

chunks.title: Palette
chunks.text:
## Palette
System r/g/b ports hold four 4-bit nibbles each. Color *i* takes
nibble (i==0||i==2 ? 4:0) of byte (i<2 ? low : high); channels expand
by duplication (`0xB → 0xBB`). Demo theme `45163, 32876, 16508`
decodes to grey-blue `#666677`, pale `#bbcccc`, brown `#bb8844`,
black `#000000`. Any theme is legal — that is the whole color story.

chunks.title: Controller / Mouse
chunks.text:
## Controller / Mouse
* Button byte bitmask (d-pad above); `key` = last keycode, self-clearing.
* Mouse `x/y` track always, `state` bitmask, scroll ports are one-shot
  deltas with inverted Y (zeroed after the vector fires).

chunks.title: Audio (4 voices, Audio0–3)
chunks.text:
## Audio (4 voices, Audio0–3)
* `pitch` = MIDI note (69 ≈ 441Hz, 0–107 audible, 108+ silent);
  high bit set = one-shot, clear = loop.
* Samples: unsigned 8-bit mono 44100Hz, 128-center. `length` in bytes,
  `volume` byte, `adsr` envelope. Long samples play ~1:1 at middle C.
* Web emulator (uxn5) has no audio device — builds play silently there.

chunks.title: System / DateTime / File
chunks.text:
## System / DateTime / File
* `System.r/g/b` theme the palette; `System.vector` boots.
  `metadata` blob carries title/author.
* DateTime ports seed RNG. File pages do host I/O relative to the
  emulator CWD (native: inline in DEO; web: completes via vector).
